mrr_or_arr: $100K-$150K MRR, peaked $150K (87% margin), stabilized ~$100K/mo mid-2026 per https://inspectural.com/blog/levelsio-photoai-single-file-php/
pricing_model: one-time credit packs + subscription tiers, self-serve checkout
why_it_worked: Existing large personal audience (Twitter/X, prior products Nomad List/Remote OK) converted cold-start into instant distribution; single-file PHP stack kept iteration speed extreme; public build-in-public revenue updates created ongoing free marketing loop.
failure_modes: 70 prior failed/shut-down startups before this hit
revenue is volatile month to month (self-reported records are 'one good day, not a new floor')
distribution channel (personal following) is not replicable without years of prior public building

case_name: Marc Lou micro-SaaS portfolio (ShipFast, DataFast, TrustMRR, CodeFast)
product: Dev boilerplate (ShipFast) + analytics (DataFast) + affiliate/referral tracking (TrustMRR) + coding course (CodeFast)
pricing_model: one-time purchase (ShipFast boilerplate) transitioning portfolio-wide toward subscription + usage-fee (TrustMRR takes 3% of referred MRR)
why_it_worked: Ships a new small product every few months and cross-promotes across the whole portfolio and newsletter list; picks products with near-zero support burden (boilerplate, tracking snippets) so one person can run several simultaneously; public monthly income breakdowns double as content marketing.
failure_modes: portfolio approach spreads focus thin — most individual products stay small; aggregate is what hits real income
one-time-purchase products (ShipFast) have revenue ceilings without constant new-customer acquisition, unlike recurring subscriptions
success leans on an audience built over years of public posting, not paid acquisition

founder: Uku Täht (solo start, Marko Saric joined ~18mo in)
mrr_or_arr: $10K MRR at ~9 months after first $400 MRR milestone; $500K ARR at ~19 months; $1M ARR by 2022; ~$3.1-3.5M ARR by 2024-2025 (https://churnkey.co/subscription-heroes/how-plausible-grew-to-1m-arr-without-ads-or-investors-marko-saric-co-founder-of-plausible/)
pricing_model: tiered subscription by pageview volume, open-source + hosted
why_it_worked: Rode the GDPR/cookie-consent + privacy backlash against Google Analytics as a tailwind; open-sourcing the code built developer trust and inbound backlinks/SEO for free; content marketing (transparent blog posts on MRR growth) compounded organic search traffic over years.
failure_modes: took a genuine market tailwind (privacy regulation) that most products don't have
required ~2 years of patient compounding before reaching life-changing income; not a fast playbook
added a co-founder for marketing — pure solo-forever path is less proven here

founder: solo founder (per 2026 indie hacker playbook writeup)
pricing_model: monthly subscription, per-seat/usage tiers typical of B2B AI tools ($49-99/mo)
why_it_worked: B2B pricing at $49-99/mo needs far fewer paying customers to hit $10K+ MRR than consumer pricing; used its own product category (AI outbound) as its own acquisition channel, a natural dogfooding loop.
failure_modes: B2B sales cycles require more manual founder-led sales/demos than self-serve consumer SaaS
cold outreach as primary channel is explicitly called out by 2026 practitioners as weaker than intent-based/community channels

product: portfolio of 35 small 'boring problem' SaaS tools
why_it_worked: Deliberately targets 'boring problems' — recurring business pain points nobody discusses at conferences but with steady year-round search volume — so each app gets found via long-tail SEO with near-zero paid marketing spend; volume-of-shots-on-goal strategy means no single app needs to be a hit.
failure_modes: 82% of micro-SaaS never reach $5K/mo and 93% never reach $10K/mo per aggregate industry stats — this portfolio approach only pays off in aggregate after many failed/small attempts
maintaining 35 codebases solo implies heavy reliance on templated/boilerplate infrastructure and low per-app support burden; doesn't generalize to complex products
